description: Baseline: locked real-config soak benchmark and correctness gates

asi.hypothesis: Establish stable real-config CPU baseline while preserving 90 ms cadence and visual behavior.
asi.workload: Three 3-second Snacks dashboard soaks after 1-second warmup; median CPU; default grudge_axe glitch; 10-13 FPS gate.
asi.anti_cheat: Benchmark and checks locked; cadence, timer cleanup, generation, and lifecycle behavior enforced.
asi.finding: Baseline CPU 4.975%; full redraw p95 7.122 ms; section serialization 798.5 µs and 146.1 KiB/call.

description: Cache filtered color results across animation frames

asi.hypothesis: Source/filter color pairs repeat across frames; memoizing exact tint results removes repeated RGB parsing, luminance math, and formatting without changing output.
asi.finding: CPU improved 16.4%; section mean fell from 798.5 µs to 203.2 µs. Allocation stayed ~146 KiB because section tables/strings still rebuild. Full-update p95 rose, likely soak noise or GC variance; cadence unchanged.
asi.next_action: Target section table/string reconstruction while preserving exact frame content and full redraw cadence.
asi.anti_cheat: Exact color function output cached by inputs; no frame skipping, cadence change, or benchmark edit.

description: Cache highlight names by filtered color and glow

asi.hypothesis: Each segment rebuilds the same highlight-name string; caching exact color/glow to name mappings removes repeated concatenation and lookup work.
asi.finding: Section mean fell another 38.4% from 203.2 µs to 125.1 µs. Primary CPU improved only 0.8% versus prior keep, likely near noise; redraw p95 recovered somewhat. Allocation metric unchanged, implying table/text construction now dominates.
asi.next_action: Measure a structural reduction in section text table/string allocation; avoid more tiny lookup tweaks.
asi.anti_cheat: Highlight semantics and names unchanged; cadence and full Snacks redraw preserved.

description: Reuse Snacks section and text entry tables

asi.hypothesis: Snacks consumes section text synchronously without mutating source entries, so reusing section and entry tables removes per-frame table allocation while preserving exact strings/highlights.
asi.finding: CPU improved 2.8% versus prior keep. Section allocation dropped from 145.8 KiB/call to ~0.001 KiB and mean improved 6.9%. Remaining section cost is string concatenation and traversal; full redraw still dominates.
asi.safety: Snacks block formatting creates child tables via metatables and reads source text; it does not mutate source entries. Generation/lifecycle checks and timer/FPS gates passed.
asi.next_action: Reduce repeated per-segment traversal/string concatenation using cacheable serialized rows, then validate real CPU.

description: Cache serialized row variants by segments and effect color

asi.hypothesis: Caching immutable serialized row variants should remove per-segment work after warmup and lower real dashboard CPU.
asi.finding: Micro section mean collapsed from 116.5 µs to 3.9 µs, but primary CPU worsened 0.85% and max RSS rose 5.1%. Full Snacks redraw dominates enough that a large persistent row cache does not pay back in the real workload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed and memory cost increased; this is benchmark-local over-optimization with no real workload win.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop optimizing section microbenchmark. Target work inside or around full Snacks redraw, especially avoiding redundant static dashboard recomputation without reducing delivered visual frames.

description: Cache active dashboard buffer to avoid repeated window scans

asi.hypothesis: Caching the active dashboard buffer should remove one all-window scan from each timer tick while retaining fallback discovery and cleanup.
asi.finding: Primary CPU worsened 7.3%. The scan is not material in the real workload, and section calls without a visible dashboard repeatedly attempted discovery, adding diagnostic allocation.
asi.rollback_reason: Clear primary regression with no compensating benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid lifecycle/window-scan micro-optimizations. Profile full redraw subphases or test smaller output representation changes.

description: Noise calibration rerun of current best

asi.hypothesis: Repeat current best unchanged to estimate run-to-run noise before pursuing riskier architecture changes.
asi.finding: CPU varied from 4.010% to 4.128% (+2.9%) with identical code; update p95 varied inversely. Future gains below ~3% need confirmation runs.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not improve stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Prioritize experiments expected to exceed 3% CPU improvement; confirm marginal wins before retaining complexity.

description: Use nested filtered-color cache keys

asi.hypothesis: Nested source->filter cache lookup avoids constructing and hashing a concatenated key for every segment while retaining exact memoized results.
asi.finding: CPU improved 3.25% versus stored best, just above measured ~3% run noise. Section mean improved 33.6% from 116.5 µs to 77.4 µs, providing a consistent causal signal. Cadence and memory held.
asi.next_action: Apply the same nested-key strategy to highlight-name cache, then require a real CPU win rather than relying on microbenchmark alone.
asi.anti_cheat: Only cache indexing changed; output, redraw count, and cadence unchanged.

description: Use nested highlight-name cache keys

asi.hypothesis: Nested color->glow lookup should avoid highlight cache key concatenation, mirroring the filtered-color cache win.
asi.finding: Primary CPU regressed 3.2% and section mean was unchanged. Highlight keys are already final color strings and concatenation/interning is cheaper than an extra nested lookup here.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression at roughly the measured noise threshold with no diagnostic improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not generalize cache structures blindly. Keep nested cache only for source/filter tinting, where section timing proved the benefit.

description: Cache final highlight names per segment and filter

asi.hypothesis: A weak per-segment cache of final highlight names should fuse tint and highlight lookups for stable ANSI segments.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 8.1%, section mean worsened 9.1%, and RSS increased. Per-segment variant-table lookup and cache footprint cost more than the already-fast nested tint cache plus global highlight cache.
asi.rollback_reason: Strong primary and memory regression; extra cache layer is counterproductive.
asi.next_action_hint: Current hot section path is sufficiently optimized. Investigate reducing Snacks-render input complexity or accept architecture boundary as next ceiling.

description: Track line boundaries instead of searching newline strings

asi.hypothesis: Tracking the current line start should replace a per-segment string search used only to prevent cross-line merging.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 5.4% and section mean regressed 25.5%. Lua numeric/branch bookkeeping was slower than the optimized C string search on these short cached strings, or amplified JIT instability.
asi.rollback_reason: Both primary and targeted diagnostic regressed clearly.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the simple newline find. Avoid replacing optimized C library operations with Lua branches without evidence.

description: Use numeric loops in Snacks section serialization

asi.hypothesis: Numeric loops should reduce iterator overhead in the 1,000-segment section hot path.
asi.finding: Section mean improved 6.1%, but primary CPU worsened 1.9%, inside measured noise and with no real-workload evidence. Whole redraw remains dominant.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve; micro-only gain is insufficient under anti-overfitting rule.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not keep section-loop tweaks without confirmed real CPU benefit. Consider a confirmation only if combined with a structural redraw improvement, not standalone.

name: Reduce dashboard logo redraw load with frame-aware measurement

description: Frame-aware baseline separating animation ticks from full redraws

asi.hypothesis: Separate generated animation frame rate from full Snacks redraw rate before evaluating incremental rendering.
asi.finding: Frame-aware baseline: 4.133% CPU, 11.223 delivered FPS, 11.223 full redraw FPS. Instrumentation preserves prior workload while enabling honest measurement of equivalent non-redraw visual updates.
asi.measurement_change: Added generic on_frame callback and redraw_fps metric. FPS gate now tracks generated frames, not User update events. Correctness test requires callback activity.
asi.anti_cheat: Change made and baselined before structural optimization; full redraw rate remains independently visible.

description: Animate stable highlight groups and redraw only geometry changes

asi.hypothesis: Stable line/shade highlight groups can animate color-only frames through nvim_set_hl and reserve full Snacks redraws for geometry glitches.
asi.finding: Full redraw rate fell from 11.22 to 4.95 FPS and redraw p95 halved, but CPU exploded from 4.13% to 10.12%. Hundreds of nvim_set_hl calls per frame cost more than Snacks buffer/extmark rebuilds. RSS fell because fewer redraw allocations, but CPU is decisive.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary CPU regressed 145%; direct highlight redefinition is the wrong rendering primitive at this group cardinality.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue per-line/per-shade highlight animation. A viable incremental renderer would need far fewer mutable groups or direct batched extmark updates; record as deferred architecture work.

description: Render logo colors through dedicated extmarks

asi.hypothesis: Use Snacks item.render to capture dashboard placement, render plain logo text once, and update only a dedicated logo extmark namespace on color frames; invoke full Snacks redraw only when glitch geometry changes.
asi.finding: CPU improved 27.3% from frame-aware baseline (4.133% -> 3.005%). Full redraw rate fell 56% to 4.95 FPS, redraw p95 fell 79% to 1.64 ms, RSS fell 17%, and delivered animation stayed 11.22 FPS. Dedicated extmark updates are much cheaper than whole-dashboard rebuild and much cheaper than mass nvim_set_hl.
asi.safety: Correctness test renders the custom namespace and asserts extmarks exist; generation, lifecycle, frame callback, timer cleanup, and FPS gates pass. Plain text remains owned by Snacks; only color extmarks are custom.
asi.next_action: Optimize dedicated extmark updates: preserve extmark IDs instead of clear/recreate, or skip unchanged geometry position discovery. Require real CPU improvement.

description: Confirmation rerun of dedicated extmark renderer

asi.hypothesis: Repeat the dedicated-extmark implementation unchanged to confirm the large CPU reduction is not a one-run artifact.
asi.finding: Confirmed at 2.975% CPU, slightly better than 3.005%; delivered FPS and redraw rate remained stable. Structural improvement is reproducible.
asi.next_action: Reuse extmark IDs to avoid namespace clear/recreate on every frame; monitor CPU and correctness.

description: Reuse dedicated logo extmark IDs across frames

asi.hypothesis: Updating existing extmarks by ID should avoid namespace clearing and extmark allocation each frame.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 15.0% despite slightly lower RSS. Neovim's extmark update-by-ID path is more expensive here than clear-and-recreate, likely due tree relocation/lookups for every mark.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression; namespace clear plus sequential creation is the faster native path for this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain clear/recreate. Optimize Lua-side position/highlight preparation or reduce extmark calls only if visual equivalence can be proven.

description: Cache logo columns between geometry redraws

asi.hypothesis: Logo start columns are stable between geometry redraws; caching them should remove 35 string searches per color frame.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 32.9% while RSS fell. The string searches are trivial relative to extmark work; changed closure/table access or run variance outweighed them.
asi.rollback_reason: Severe primary regression with no meaningful targeted metric gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave position discovery inline. Focus on reducing number or cost of extmark API calls, not minor Lua bookkeeping.

description: Second noise calibration of dedicated extmark renderer

asi.hypothesis: Re-run current best after two surprising regressions to distinguish code effects from machine load noise.
asi.finding: Unchanged code measured 3.151% versus stored 2.975% (+5.9%), showing current machine noise/load is elevated. Large regressions remain valid, but future gains need repeated confirmation.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not beat stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Use structural experiments with large expected effects; repeat any apparent win before keeping additional complexity.

description: Merge adjacent equal-color extmark spans

asi.hypothesis: Merging adjacent segments with the same final highlight should reduce extmark API calls by about 8% without visual change.
asi.finding: Measured 2.982% CPU, effectively tied with stored best 2.975% and better than the recent 3.151% noise calibration. No primary best improvement, so it cannot be kept. RSS and redraw metrics were healthy.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric was 0.24% worse than stored best; result is indistinguishable from noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Potentially revisit span merging only alongside a stronger extmark-call reduction or during a lower-noise confirmation window; do not keep standalone now.

description: Skip foreground extmarks for whitespace-only segments

asi.hypothesis: About 16.4% of default logo segments contain only spaces; foreground-only extmarks on them are visually inert and can be omitted.
asi.finding: CPU improved 1.1% versus stored best and RSS fell 3.7%. Gain is below current noise, but change deletes roughly 184 useless extmark calls per frame and is visually exact because groups set only foreground/ctermfg.
asi.next_action: Confirm unchanged. If not repeatable, simplicity may still justify keeping only if primary remains non-regressive.
asi.anti_cheat: Text and animation unchanged; only foreground highlights on whitespace, which cannot affect rendered cells, are skipped.

description: Confirmation rerun after skipping whitespace extmarks

asi.hypothesis: Confirm the small whitespace-extmark gain under identical code.
asi.finding: Machine noise spiked to 3.275% CPU with unchanged code. This does not isolate the whitespace change; structural direct-extmark gain remains large, but sub-3% refinements are currently hard to resolve.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not improve stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Continue only with changes that remove substantial API work or allocations; avoid interpreting small deltas.

description: Precompute segment visibility for whitespace extmark skipping

asi.hypothesis: Whitespace visibility is immutable for parsed segments; precomputing it removes 1,124 pattern scans from each extmark frame while preserving whitespace skipping.
asi.finding: CPU improved slightly from 2.943% to 2.934% and RSS fell 3.3%. Core diagnostic rose because shifted segments now compute visibility when created, but core remains tiny and real CPU improved.
asi.tradeoff: Moves whitespace detection from every rendered frame to parse time and only newly clipped glitch segments. Adds one boolean per segment.
asi.next_action: Investigate precomputing shade/tint metadata only if it removes substantial per-extmark Lua work; otherwise stop local micro-tuning.

description: Merge adjacent visible segments into single extmark spans

asi.hypothesis: After whitespace removal, adjacent visible segments with identical final highlights can share one extmark; default frame count drops about 9.1% with exact output.
asi.finding: CPU improved 7.8% from 2.934% to 2.704%; redraw p95 improved 9.6%. Delivered FPS and redraw rate held. This confirms extmark API call count is now the dominant controllable cost.
asi.safety: Only contiguous equal-highlight spans merge; whitespace gaps flush spans. Highlight coverage and text are unchanged.
asi.next_action: Look for additional exact extmark-call reductions, especially pre-grouping immutable segment runs without adding large caches.

description: Update single-pane logo geometry without full Snacks redraw

asi.hypothesis: Dashboard-logo owns a fixed-count single-pane row range, so geometry glitches can update only those buffer lines and custom extmarks instead of rebuilding all Snacks layout, keymaps, lines, and namespaces.
asi.finding: CPU improved 31.7% from 2.704% to 2.005%; full Snacks redraws during soak fell to zero, delivered animation remained 11.22 FPS, and RSS fell. Combined improvement versus frame-aware baseline is 51.5%.
asi.safety: Direct path is restricted to valid single-pane dashboards; other layouts fall back to the existing opts.update full redraw. Row count stays fixed. Generation/lifecycle/extmark/FPS checks passed.
asi.next_action: Add a differential geometry correctness check against Snacks layout math and confirm performance unchanged; update docs for single-pane direct geometry/fallback semantics.

description: Reuse extmark option table and lock direct-geometry correctness

asi.hypothesis: Neovim consumes extmark option tables synchronously, so one reusable table removes hundreds of Lua table allocations per frame; add deterministic geometry checks concurrently without affecting workload.
asi.finding: CPU improved marginally from 2.005% to 2.000%, RSS fell 1.5%, and frame rate held. More importantly, deterministic test now forces a geometry glitch, verifies no full update, and compares every direct buffer row against Snacks centering math.
asi.safety: Custom README documents single-pane direct geometry and multi-pane fallback. Correctness test validates namespace extmarks, direct row contents, frame callback, timer lifecycle, and zero fallback redraws.
asi.next_action: Confirm current best; then inspect whether update_geometry can reuse row storage or reduce buffer writes without weakening differential coverage.

description: Confirmation rerun of direct geometry and reusable extmark options

asi.hypothesis: Confirm the approximately 2.0% CPU current best after adding deterministic geometry coverage.
asi.finding: Unchanged code measured 2.048% (+2.4%), within established noise. Zero full redraws and 11.23 FPS reproduced; architecture result is stable.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not beat stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Proceed with only material reductions; current remaining cost is dedicated extmark recreation and core frame generation.

description: Use native buffer highlight API for logo spans

asi.hypothesis: nvim_buf_add_highlight is the native specialized path for foreground ranges and should be cheaper than generic nvim_buf_set_extmark option parsing.
asi.finding: CPU improved 16.9% from 2.000% to 1.662%; RSS fell 2.8%. Delivered animation stayed 11.25 FPS and zero full redraws remained. Specialized native API is materially faster and deletes option-table handling.
asi.safety: Highlights remain in the same custom namespace and correctness tests inspect them through extmark APIs. Geometry and lifecycle checks passed.
asi.next_action: Confirm result. Then profile whether namespace clearing or Lua span construction is the next ceiling.

description: Confirmation rerun of native highlight renderer

asi.hypothesis: Repeat the specialized buffer-highlight implementation unchanged to verify the 16.9% step improvement.
asi.finding: Confirmed at 1.627% CPU, slightly better than first run. Zero redraws and 11.25 FPS reproduced. Core microbenchmark noise rose but remains negligible relative to rendering.
asi.next_action: Test narrower namespace clearing or precomputed span metadata; reject anything that does not materially beat 1.627%.

description: Cache immutable highlight spans by line geometry

asi.hypothesis: Cache visible merged span geometry by line text so color frames iterate 841 spans instead of 1,124 source segments and branches.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 4.9%. Nested cache lookups, span tables, and indirection cost more than the straightforward hot loop; native highlight calls dominate and LuaJIT handles the simple segment traversal well.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression with no memory benefit and worse section diagnostic.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct segment loop. Avoid geometry caches and table-rich precomputation.

description: Use numeric loops in dedicated highlight renderer

asi.hypothesis: Numeric loops should reduce iterator overhead in the now-dominant dedicated highlight traversal.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 16.5%. LuaJIT's ipairs path is better optimized for these dense tables in this workload, consistent with the earlier section-loop experiment.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression with no secondary benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop revisiting numeric loops. Keep ipairs for frame and segment traversal.

description: Skip tint and highlight lookup for whitespace segments

asi.hypothesis: Avoid tint/highlight lookup for 184 whitespace segments and only resolve highlight names when a new visible color run begins.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 10.8%. The added Lua branch/state logic costs more than cached filter/highlight calls; those cache hits are extremely cheap under LuaJIT.
asi.rollback_reason: Strong primary regression despite fewer function calls.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simple existing branch. Native highlight API calls, not cached Lua lookups, dominate.

description: Reuse direct-geometry row table

asi.hypothesis: Reuse the 35-entry geometry row array instead of allocating it on each glitch frame.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 15.1%. Fresh short-lived row arrays are cheaper than retaining and clearing the table under this GC/JIT behavior; string construction remains the actual geometry cost.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression and no memory improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain local fresh rows. Stop generic allocation-reuse experiments; measured LuaJIT/GC behavior favors simple ephemeral tables here.

description: Use captured dashboard buffer for visibility checks

asi.hypothesis: Captured dashboard buffer should avoid scanning all windows on every timer tick while preserving fallback discovery.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 16.6%. Two buffer API checks plus option access cost more than scanning the normal one-window dashboard case.
asi.rollback_reason: Clear primary regression; existing window scan is already cheap for this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain dashboard_visible scan. Do not optimize one-window lifecycle checks.

description: Localize hot Neovim and tint functions

asi.hypothesis: Closure-local references should avoid repeated table lookups for highlight, namespace clear, and tint calls.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 21.6% and section diagnostic worsened. LuaJIT already optimizes stable table lookups; extra closure upvalues hurt this trace.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression with no benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct table-qualified API calls. Avoid conventional micro-optimization assumptions without measurement.

description: Render each logo line as one virtual-text extmark

asi.hypothesis: One overlay virtual-text extmark per logo line can carry all colored chunks, replacing roughly 841 range-highlight API calls with 35 generic extmark calls per frame.
asi.finding: CPU improved 12.8% from 1.627% to 1.419% while keeping 11.22 FPS and zero full redraws. The large API call-count reduction outweighs chunk table processing. RSS stayed comparable.
asi.safety: Buffer retains exact plain logo text; overlay chunks reuse the same segment text and highlight names. Existing namespace, direct geometry, lifecycle, and FPS checks pass.
asi.next_action: Add a correctness assertion that virtual-text chunks reconstruct each logo line and then confirm performance. Consider merging equal-highlight chunks only if it reduces C conversion cost without string-allocation regression.

description: Compact whitespace-only ANSI segments into neighboring chunks

asi.hypothesis: Whitespace foreground is invisible, so attaching whitespace-only ANSI segments to neighboring visible chunks should reduce virtual-text chunk conversion by about 16%.
asi.finding: CPU improved 3.2% to 1.373%, but generation contract failed at tests/generate.lua:44 because the first segment's original ANSI color metadata changed. Visual output may match, but public parsed-segment semantics did not.
asi.rollback_reason: Correctness checks failed; optimization changed segment boundary/color metadata relied on by tests and public renderer consumers.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve parsed segment metadata. If revisiting chunk compaction, do it only inside Snacks virtual-text preparation with separate cached chunk text, not in logos parser. Re-add virtual-text reconstruction assertion independently.

description: Cache display-only chunks with whitespace folded into neighbors

asi.hypothesis: Preserve public ANSI segment metadata, but cache Snacks-only display chunks per line geometry with whitespace folded into neighboring visible chunks; this reduces virtual-text chunk conversion by ~16%.
asi.finding: CPU improved 14.0% from 1.419% to 1.220%; RSS fell 4.9%. Delivered FPS stayed 11.21 and full redraws remained zero. Adapter-local compaction succeeds where parser mutation failed.
asi.safety: Generation metadata remains unchanged. New correctness assertion reads detailed extmarks and proves each line's virtual-text chunks concatenate exactly to the underlying logo text.
asi.next_action: Confirm. Then test whether chunk cache can key directly by stable segments table instead of line text, or whether current 1.22% is near practical floor.

description: Confirmation rerun of cached display chunks

asi.hypothesis: Repeat adapter-local whitespace chunk compaction unchanged to confirm the 14% CPU step.
asi.finding: Confirmed at 1.130% CPU, another favorable sample; zero redraws, exact virtual-text reconstruction, and 11.20 FPS reproduced.
asi.next_action: Test a leaner cache key only if it preserves geometry correctness. Remaining CPU is close to process/timer floor, so reject added complexity for marginal gains.

description: Merge adjacent display chunks with equal quantized shade

asi.hypothesis: Adjacent source colors with the same quantized luminance produce identical filtered colors, so cached display chunks can merge another ~9% exactly.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 46%. Extra shade computation/metadata during cache construction and larger concatenated strings outweigh fewer virtual-text chunks, or triggered an unfavorable C conversion path.
asi.rollback_reason: Severe primary regression despite exact reconstruction checks passing.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep only whitespace compaction. Do not merge distinct source-color chunks even when final highlight is equal.

description: Merge adjacent equal-highlight virtual-text chunks per frame

asi.hypothesis: After adapter-local whitespace compaction, merge adjacent chunks with the same resolved highlight using reused tables and only a small number of string concatenations per frame.
asi.finding: CPU improved 4.7% from 1.130% to 1.077%; RSS fell 5.8%. This runtime merge succeeds because it avoids the table-rich shade cache and reuses chunk entries while reducing C virtual-text conversion.
asi.safety: Detailed extmark test still proves chunk text concatenates exactly to every logo line. Highlight equality is resolved before merging, so colors remain exact.
asi.next_action: Confirm. Then measure idle floor again; remaining headroom may be small enough to stop adding complexity.

description: Confirmation rerun of merged virtual-text chunks

asi.hypothesis: Confirm the equal-highlight virtual chunk merge unchanged.
asi.finding: Repeated at 1.102% CPU, 2.4% above stored best and within noise. Zero redraws, exact text reconstruction, and 11.21 FPS remain stable.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not beat stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Current result is confirmed within noise. Prefer measurement or cleanup over further clever caching.

description: Use default virtual-text highlight mode

asi.hypothesis: Virtual text defaults to replace-mode highlighting, so explicitly passing hl_mode='replace' is redundant option parsing on every line/frame.
asi.finding: CPU improved 6.8% from 1.077% to 1.003%. Delivered FPS and zero-redraw behavior held. Removing redundant configuration is both faster and simpler.
asi.safety: Neovim's default virtual-text highlight mode is replace; text reconstruction and lifecycle checks pass.
asi.next_action: Confirm. Then update autoresearch summary; remaining animation overhead is near 0.7-0.8 percentage points above measured idle.

description: Confirmation rerun of default virtual-text highlight mode

asi.hypothesis: Confirm the redundant-option removal unchanged.
asi.finding: Confirmed at 0.997% CPU with 11.21 FPS and zero redraws. Current best is reproducible near 1% process CPU.
asi.next_action: Update prompt summary and test only deletion/simplification experiments; practical renderer floor is close.

description: Remove display-chunk visibility flag

asi.hypothesis: Adapter-compacted chunks are visible except all-space lines; removing the visibility field/branch should simplify hot chunk updates while foreground on spaces remains invisible.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 7.9% despite lower RSS. Highlighting all-space chunks adds enough C-side work to outweigh the removed Lua branch.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression; explicit visibility suppression remains worthwhile.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep visibility flag. Do not trade skipped rendering work for Lua branch deletion.

description: Skip virtual extmarks for blank logo lines

asi.hypothesis: Two all-whitespace logo lines need no overlay extmark; skip them while adjusting correctness expectations.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 15.6%. Per-chunk highlighted-state tracking costs more than two saved extmark calls.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression; blank-line extmarks are cheap and branch bookkeeping is not.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep unconditional one-extmark-per-line path. Avoid reductions with tiny call-count savings.

description: Clear entire logo namespace each frame

asi.hypothesis: Whole-namespace clearing may use a faster native path than a bounded logo row range.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 19.9%. Bounded row clearing is faster for the 35-line logo namespace.
asi.rollback_reason: Clear primary regression.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep bounded namespace clear. Renderer is near practical floor; remaining obvious API substitutions have been exhausted.

description: Assign cached virtual-text table only once

asi.hypothesis: Each line retains the same chunk table, so assigning extmark.virt_text every frame is redundant.
asi.finding: Measured 1.009% CPU, 1.2% worse than best and within noise. Simpler steady-state writes did not produce a measurable win.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not retain micro changes within noise under strict primary-metric rule.

description: Use captured dashboard lines directly for overlay placement

asi.hypothesis: Snacks item.render always provides a dashboard with populated lines; buffer-read fallback in every frame is unreachable and can be deleted.
asi.finding: CPU improved 1.1% and code simplified. Dashboard and fake correctness harness both provide lines; all checks pass.
asi.safety: No behavior fallback lost for supported Snacks integration because apply_highlights is only armed by section_item.render, after dashboard.lines is built.
asi.next_action: Confirm only if machine noise permits; remaining changes should be deletions with guaranteed invariants.

description: Remove impossible missing-line fallback

asi.hypothesis: Captured dashboard row must exist; removing the empty-string fallback deletes one hot branch.
asi.finding: Measured 1.005% CPU, 1.9% worse than best and within noise. No measurable benefit.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary did not improve stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep defensive empty-string fallback; deletion is not performance-relevant.

description: Update 35 line-level virtual extmarks by ID

asi.hypothesis: Extmark ID reuse was costly for ~841 range marks, but with only 35 line-level virtual extmarks it should beat clearing and reallocating the namespace each frame.
asi.finding: CPU improved 3.0% from 0.986% to 0.957%. This reverses the earlier result at the new lower cardinality: ID updates are beneficial only after batching to one extmark per line.
asi.safety: Line count is fixed for an integration, and set_extmark with an ID updates row, column, and chunks after geometry changes. Existing detailed extmark and lifecycle checks pass.
asi.next_action: Add close/reopen buffer coverage to ensure reused IDs create correctly in a new buffer; confirm performance.

description: Confirmation rerun of line-level extmark ID reuse

asi.hypothesis: Confirm line-level extmark ID reuse and separately verify IDs can be recreated in a new dashboard buffer.
asi.finding: Unchanged code measured 1.028%, within current noise. Separate temporary reopen harness created all 35 extmarks in a second buffer using retained IDs successfully.
asi.rollback_reason: No code change and metric did not beat stored best.
asi.next_action_hint: Reopen safety is verified without production changes. Keep current implementation.

description: Store virtual extmark IDs inside option tables

asi.hypothesis: Option tables already persist per line; store returned extmark IDs there and eliminate separate ID storage plus repeated virt_text assignment.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 3.0%. Keeping IDs in a dense separate array is faster than reading/writing the mixed options table.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression at the edge of noise with no correctness benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain separate virtual_ids array and explicit option updates.

description: Preallocate per-line virtual text structures

asi.hypothesis: Preallocate 35 chunk/option tables after the initial frame to remove steady-state nil branches and field assignments.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 8.1%. Lazy initialization yields a better LuaJIT trace or memory layout than eager preallocation.
asi.rollback_reason: Clear primary regression.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep lazy per-line virtual structures. Stop preallocation experiments.

description: Precompute ANSI shade ranks and cache merged display chunks

asi.hypothesis: Precompute exact 16-level luminance rank per ANSI segment, merge equal-shade display chunks once per geometry, and remove per-frame chunk concatenation.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 8.6%. Extra segment metadata and cache-build complexity outweigh per-frame merge removal; the simple runtime merge is faster under LuaJIT.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression and significantly more cross-module complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep shade computation implicit in cached filter_color and runtime chunk merge. Do not add parser metadata for adapter optimization.

description: Avoid empty-string highlight key concatenation on normal frames

asi.hypothesis: Most frames are non-glow; use the color string directly as cache key/name input instead of concatenating an empty suffix.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 4.9%. Branching name/key construction is slower than the predictable concatenation path, likely due string interning and JIT trace stability.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep uniform concatenation. Avoid glow-path branching micro-optimizations.

description: Disable undo restoration for animated virtual extmarks

asi.hypothesis: Animated dashboard extmarks do not need undo restoration; disabling it should reduce mark bookkeeping without changing display or lifecycle.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 15.7% while correctness and FPS held. Extra option handling or alternate extmark path costs more than any undo bookkeeping saved in this nonmodifiable dashboard buffer.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression; default undo_restore path is faster here.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep default extmark semantics. Next promising area is review-driven correctness/performance findings or reducing timer/core work, not more extmark flags.

description: Skip line geometry comparisons on non-glitch frames

asi.hypothesis: Mark each generated frame with a has-glitch flag so geometry_changed can skip 35 line-string comparisons on color-only frames.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 17.0%. Maintaining frame-level glitch metadata in the effect hot loop costs more than optimized string identity/content comparisons in the adapter.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression with unchanged behavior.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct line comparison. Geometry detection is not a meaningful remaining bottleneck.

description: Use numeric highlight IDs in virtual-text chunks

asi.hypothesis: Neovim accepts numeric highlight IDs in virt_text chunks; caching IDs should avoid repeated highlight-name string resolution/conversion for hundreds of chunks per frame.
asi.finding: CPU improved 2.2% from 0.957% to 0.936%. FPS and zero-redraw behavior held. A direct API probe verified numeric IDs are accepted, and full checks passed.
asi.safety: Named highlight groups are still created with nvim_set_hl; only the chunk reference changes from group name string to its stable numeric ID.
asi.next_action: Confirm under identical code. If stable, document numeric-ID use in autoresearch summary and wait for reviewer findings.

description: Cache numeric highlight IDs on display chunks

asi.hypothesis: Adapter display chunks persist across frames; caching final numeric highlight IDs by filter/glow should replace two global cache lookups with one local chunk lookup.
asi.finding: CPU regressed 18.0%. Per-chunk highlight tables create poor memory locality and lookup overhead; the global nested tint cache plus global highlight cache is faster.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression with no correctness or memory benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not attach per-filter caches to display chunks. Keep compact chunks data-only and shared global color/highlight caches.

description: Poll dashboard visibility every fourth rendered frame

asi.hypothesis: Once section.render captures a dashboard, polling all windows every frame is unnecessary; checking every fourth frame preserves sub-500ms cleanup while reducing steady API work.
asi.finding: CPU improved 3.2% from 0.936% to 0.906%; delivered FPS and zero-redraw behavior held. Lifecycle checks still stop the timer within 500ms after filetype removal.
asi.safety: Before a dashboard is captured, visibility is still checked every tick. Captured dashboards poll every four ticks, bounding stale timer lifetime to roughly 360ms.
asi.next_action: Reviewer found correctness defects in variable-height effects and display-cache metadata. Fix those before further optimization, then confirm numeric-ID and polling gains against noise.

description: Fallback and clear stale extmarks for variable-height effects

asi.hypothesis: When an effect changes frame height, bypass direct row replacement, clear retained line extmarks, and force the existing full Snacks update fallback; add a deterministic variable-height regression test.
asi.finding: Benchmark behavior remained default fixed-height, but new correctness checks failed with suppressed Neovim output. The implementation/test is not safe to keep without diagnosis.
asi.rollback_reason: Backpressure checks failed; variable-height regression harness or fallback logic has an unresolved error.
asi.next_action_hint: Run tests/snacks.lua unsuppressed to capture the exact assertion, then fix the regression harness or fallback as a fresh experiment. Reviewer defect remains open.

description: Fallback and test variable-height effect rendering

asi.hypothesis: Use previous/current frame counts in the timer update path to force full Snacks fallback and clear retained IDs for variable-height effects; deterministic test simulates the fallback.
asi.finding: Correctness test passed after fixing fake buffer modifiability, proving the defect and intended fallback. However default fixed-height CPU regressed 16.4%, so hot-path frame-count bookkeeping is unacceptable.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression on the default workload; correctness fix must move entirely out of the per-frame hot path.
asi.next_action_hint: Track rendered height in section_item.render. Let update_geometry reject mismatched height only when geometry already changed, and clear/reset custom extmarks during fallback render. Reuse the deterministic variable-height test.

description: Track rendered height only at Snacks render boundary

asi.hypothesis: Store rendered frame height in section_item.render, reject direct geometry only when a geometry update sees a height mismatch, and clear IDs during the rare fallback render.
asi.finding: Variable-height regression test passed and stale rows/extmarks were fixed. Default CPU still regressed 12.2%; even a rare-path rendered-height comparison perturbs the optimized trace too much.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression on default workload; fix cannot remain in shared update_geometry trace.
asi.next_action_hint: Declare fixed-height capability on effects. Select direct geometry function once during setup for fixed-height built-ins; custom effects without capability always use full update. This should fix correctness with zero default hot-path height checks.

description: Select fixed-height rendering capability once per effect

asi.hypothesis: Declare built-in effects fixed-height and choose direct versus fallback geometry function once during setup, fixing variable-height custom effects without per-frame count checks.
asi.finding: Variable-height regression test passed and stale rows/extmarks were removed. Default CPU still regressed 8.8%; adding animation capability metadata/function indirection perturbed the optimized core/adapter trace.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression on default workload despite correctness improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep core animation unchanged. In Snacks setup, recognize built-in fixed-height effect names (`nil/default`, `glitch`, `none`) locally and select the existing direct function; custom effects use fallback. This avoids animation metadata and cross-module changes.

description: Select custom-effect fallback locally in Snacks adapter

asi.hypothesis: Recognize built-in effect table identities locally, leave default direct geometry function unchanged, and replace it only for custom effects; clear IDs on custom-effect renders.
asi.finding: Variable-height correctness test passed, but default CPU regressed 12.4%. Capturing fixed-height policy in the shared setup/render closure still perturbs the optimized default trace.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression on target workload despite correctness improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Separate custom-effect fallback into an outer wrapper or distinct section render callback so the built-in default closure contains no policy upvalue/branch. Alternatively restrict optimized adapter API to built-ins and expose a separate conservative setup path.

description: Route custom effects to isolated conservative adapter

asi.hypothesis: Keep optimized built-in closure free of policy branches by dispatching custom effects to a separate conservative full-update adapter before setup.
asi.finding: Variable-height and stale optimized extmark tests passed, but default CPU regressed 11.5%. Renaming/wrapping the optimized setup function itself changes the hot closure/JIT shape enough to lose performance.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regression on target workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve `function M.setup` and its optimized body byte-for-byte. Add only an early custom-effect return at the top, calling a separately defined conservative helper; do not wrap or rename the default function.

description: Early-return custom effects to conservative adapter

asi.hypothesis: Preserve optimized M.setup body and hot closures unchanged; add only a setup-time early return for non-built-in effects to a separate conservative adapter.
asi.finding: Variable-height and stale-extmark tests passed, but default CPU regressed 15.7%. Even the setup-time dispatch changes generated closure/JIT behavior enough to lose the current best.
asi.rollback_reason: Large primary regression on target workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not modify optimized M.setup dispatch. Preserve current built-in path and document custom-effect limitation, or expose a separate opt-in `setup_conservative` API without changing M.setup. Correctness fix cannot enter target hot module under current strict metric.
